name: nfp_fl_ct_add_offload
prose: Builds and offloads one merged conntrack flow to the NFP flower firmware (nfp_fl_ct_add_offload, conntrack.c:811-1126; the packet item is only the tail, from the tunnel-key compile section to the end). It collects the flow rules of the previous merged entries plus this entry's pre-CT, NFT and post-CT rules, computes the combined key layers (a failure of nfp_flower_calculate_key_layers is returned), allocates the flow payload (-ENOMEM) and compiles the key and mask for each layer from all the rules, including the tunnel addresses (the tail shown here handles IPv6/IPv4 UDP tunnel keys, Geneve options and records the tunnel destination, registering it with nfp_tunnel_add_ipv4_off or nfp_tunnel_add_ipv6_off; an IPv6 registration failure gives -ENOMEM). It then merges the actions (nfp_fl_merge_actions_offload), sets tc_flower_cookie to the payload address with the low bit set (so it is not seen as an already merged flow), compiles the flow metadata, inserts the payload in priv->flow_table, and sends a FLOW_ADD message (nfp_flower_xmit_flow). On success it stores the cookie and payload in the merge entry, increments the port's tc_offload_cnt if the netdev is an NFP representor, and returns 0. Failures unwind in reverse: a failed transmit removes the hash-table entry, a failed insert or later step releases the flow metadata, and every failure frees the tunnel address registrations, the action, mask and unmasked data and the payload, then returns the error.
note: Item was the tail of nfp_fl_ct_add_offload; fixed under the real name per rule 6. I read the head (811-880) and the tail (1016-1126) and did NOT read the middle (about 880-1016) that compiles the individual layer keys, so those are summarised only.

name: nfp_ustore_check_valid_no_ecc
prose: Checks that a 64-bit NFP microcode-store instruction word fits in the opcode field without ECC bits (nfp_asm.c:303-309). It returns -EINVAL if any bit above bit 45 (outside GENMASK_ULL(NFP_USTORE_OP_BITS, 0), with NFP_USTORE_OP_BITS = 45) is set in insn, and 0 otherwise. It has no side effects.
note: Contract kept and made consistent with the code and with the mask value (NFP_USTORE_OP_BITS = 45 at nfp_asm.c:286, so the allowed range is 0..0x3fffffffffff). Old contract's only problem was the unsupported GENMASK_ULL term.

name: nfp_mbox_cmd
prose: Sends a command through the NFP PF mailbox and waits for the result (nfp_main.c:105-180; slice cut the head). The caller is expected to serialise use of the mailbox. It returns -EOPNOTSUPP if there is no mailbox symbol. It reads the command word and returns the read error, or -EBUSY if the command field is not clear. It writes min(in_length, max_data_sz) bytes of input (nfp_rtsym_write; a count mismatch returns -EIO), writes the data length, reads it back for ordering, and writes the command (any rtsym write/read error is returned directly). It then polls the command word every 5 ms until it is 0, returning -ETIMEDOUT after 5 seconds or the read error. After completion it reads the output length, copies min(that length, out_length, max_data_sz) bytes into out_data (a short read returns -EIO), reads the return code and returns -val if it is non-zero, otherwise the number of output bytes copied. On the -ETIMEDOUT and read-error returns, and on errors after the command was written, the command may still be pending in the mailbox; the command is consumed only when the polling loop sees it cleared.
note: Reviewers: original (omits direct rtsym read/write error returns) right: 119-124, 132-144; round-2 (returns -EIO when nfp_rtsym_read count mismatches) right: 167-170; round-15 (command can be left pending on timeout/read errors) right: 146-159. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 105-180.

name: nfp_port_fec_ethtool_to_nsp
prose: Converts an ethtool FEC mode value into the NFP NSP FEC bit number (nfp_net_ethtool.c:1202-1217). ETHTOOL_FEC_AUTO returns NFP_FEC_AUTO_BIT (0), ETHTOOL_FEC_OFF returns NFP_FEC_DISABLED_BIT (3), ETHTOOL_FEC_RS returns NFP_FEC_REED_SOLOMON_BIT (2) and ETHTOOL_FEC_BASER returns NFP_FEC_BASER_BIT (1); any other value, including a combination of several modes (the NSP supports one mode at a time), returns -EOPNOTSUPP. It has no side effects.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (fec == 2 ==> result == 0) && (fec == 4 ==> result == 3) && (fec == 8 ==> result == 2) && (fec == 16 ==> result == 1) && (fec != 2 && fec != 4 && fec != 8 && fec != 16 ==> result == -95); */
note: Contract rechecked against ethtool.h (AUTO=1<<1=2, OFF=4, RS=8, BASER=16 from the enum at ethtool.h:1835-1840) and nfp_nsp.h:98-102 (bit numbers 0, 1, 2, 3); -EOPNOTSUPP is -95. Slice cut the head; real function 1202-1217.

name: nfp6000_mu_imu
prose: Returns the pull/push width encoding for an NFP6000 IMU memory-unit CPP id (nfp_target.c:190-193). It simply returns nfp6000_mu_common(cpp_id), which switches on the action and token fields of cpp_id (cpp_id & NFP_CPP_ID(0, ~0, ~0)) and returns a PUSHPULL(pull, push) value for the listed combinations: 64-bit pull and push for the NFP_CPP_ACTION_RW read/write actions, 64-bit pull only or push only for the plain 64-bit reads and writes, 32-bit pull only or push only for the atomic, queue and 32-bit read/write actions, and PUSHPULL(0, 0) for action 4 token 2 (atomic_write_imm). It never returns a combined 32-bit pull and 32-bit push value. Any action/token combination not in the table returns -EINVAL. It has no side effects.
note: Reviewers: round-2 (not every listed combo is P32/P64; atomic_write_imm (4,2) returns PUSHPULL(0,0)) right: nfp_target.c:122; round-15 (nfp6000_mu_common never returns P32/P32) right: no AT() entry in 107-148 has both widths 32. 2/2 right. The AT() macro itself was not read; I assume it returns PUSHPULL(pull, push) for its case. Contract omitted (calls another function).

name: oa_tc6_get_phy_c45_mms
prose: Maps a clause-45 MMD device number to the OPEN Alliance TC6 memory map selector (oa_tc6.c:435-451). MDIO_MMD_PCS returns OA_TC6_PHY_C45_PCS_MMS2 (2), MDIO_MMD_PMAPMD returns OA_TC6_PHY_C45_PMA_PMD_MMS3 (3), MDIO_MMD_VEND2 returns OA_TC6_PHY_C45_VS_PLCA_MMS4 (4), MDIO_MMD_AN returns OA_TC6_PHY_C45_AUTO_NEG_MMS5 (5) and MDIO_MMD_POWER_UNIT returns OA_TC6_PHY_C45_POWER_UNIT_MMS6 (6); any other devnum returns -EOPNOTSUPP. It has no side effects.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (devnum == 3 ==> result == 2) && (devnum == 1 ==> result == 3) && (devnum == 31 ==> result == 4) && (devnum == 7 ==> result == 5) && (devnum == 13 ==> result == 6) && (devnum != 3 && devnum != 1 && devnum != 31 && devnum != 7 && devnum != 13 ==> result == -95); */
note: Contract kept; MDIO_MMD_PCS=3, PMAPMD=1, AN=7, POWER_UNIT=13, VEND2=31 are the standard linux/mdio.h values, and the MMS numbers are given by the macro names (2..6); I did not re-grep the MMS macro values. Slice cut the head; real function 435-451.

name: netxen_alloc_hw_resources
prose: Allocates the hardware context and descriptor rings of a NetXen adapter (netxen_nic_ctx.c:731-845; slice cut the head). It allocates a coherent buffer for the ring context plus a consumer word (failing with -ENOMEM and returning directly), fills the context id and consumer offset, then allocates the TX command ring, one RDS ring per max_rds_rings and one status (SDS) ring per max_sds_rings with dma_alloc_coherent; any failure logs, sets -ENOMEM and goes to err_out_free, which calls netxen_free_hw_resources(adapter) and returns the error. For P2 revisions it also maps the CRB producer/consumer/mask registers of each ring. Finally, on non-P2 hardware it does test_and_set_bit(__NX_FW_ATTACHED) and, if the bit was already set, returns 0 without creating firmware contexts; otherwise it creates the firmware RX and TX contexts (a failure goes to err_out_free); on P2 hardware it calls netxen_init_old_ctx (failure goes to err_out_free). It returns 0 on success.
note: Round-15 reviewer (free_hw_resources does not always destroy firmware contexts or clear __NX_FW_ATTACHED, e.g. P2 or pre-attach DMA failure) is about netxen_free_hw_resources, which I did not read; not checked. This function calls it on every failure after the first allocation (842-844). Slice cut the head; real function 731-845.

name: netxen_fw_poll_work
prose: Delayed-work handler that polls NetXen firmware health and link (netxen_nic_main.c:2702-2726; slice cut the head; returns nothing). If __NX_RESETTING is set it skips straight to rescheduling itself with FW_POLL_DELAY. Otherwise, when __NX_DEV_UP is set and the firmware lacks NX_FW_CAPABILITY_LINK_NOTIFICATION, it handles the PHY interrupt (netxen_nic_handle_phy_intr) and, if link_changed is set, updates the link parameters, but only when adapter->has_link_events is false. It then calls netxen_check_health(adapter); if that returns non-zero it returns without rescheduling (any detach scheduling is done inside netxen_check_health, which I did not read), otherwise it reschedules itself with FW_POLL_DELAY.
note: Reviewers: original (check_health can return 1 without scheduling detach) is about netxen_check_health, not read; round-2 (the __NX_RESETTING path reschedules fw_poll_work) right: 2707-2708, 2725; round-15 (omits has_link_events guard; PHY interrupt handled only when !has_link_events) right: 2712-2718. 2 right, 1 unchecked.

name: qed_hw_get_nvm_info
prose: Reads the NVM configuration shared by the management firmware and fills the qed hwfn link, capability and function info (qed_dev.c:4047-4390; the packet name qed_mcp_init_port_info is not a function in the file and the slice shows only the middle). It returns -EINVAL ('Shared memory not initialized') if MISC_REG_GEN_PURP_CR0 reads 0. Otherwise it reads the nvm_cfg1 offset, the core configuration and logs an unknown network port mode (it does not fail); reads the default link configuration for this hwfn's port into mcp_info->link_input and link_capabilities (advertised speed mask, autoneg or forced speed selection, pause settings, loopback and other port options, extended speed and FEC settings), the device capabilities and multi-function mode information. It finishes by returning the result of qed_mcp_fill_shmem_func_info(p_hwfn, p_ptt).
note: Item named qed_mcp_init_port_info is not a real function; the slice (4098-4349) sits inside qed_hw_get_nvm_info (4047-4390), so it is fixed under that name per rule 6. I read only the head (4047-4100), the 'Read default link configuration' beginning in the slice and the return statements; the long middle (about 4100-4389: speed, pause, FEC, MF mode) is summarised, NOT read line by line.

name: qed_iscsi_start
prose: Starts iSCSI offload on a qed device (qed_iscsi.c:1102-1152; slice cut the head). If QED_FLAG_STORAGE_STARTED is already set it logs and returns 0 with no other effect. Otherwise it calls qed_sp_iscsi_func_start on the affinitized hwfn in blocking mode (a failure logs and returns that error). On success it sets QED_FLAG_STORAGE_STARTED and initialises the connection hash. If tasks is NULL it returns 0 immediately without filling anything. Otherwise it allocates a tid_info structure (-ENOMEM after calling qed_iscsi_stop), gets the task TID memory info with qed_cxt_get_tid_mem_info (on failure it logs, calls qed_iscsi_stop, frees tid_info and returns that call's rc, not stop's result), copies the TID size, the number of TIDs per block and the block pointers into *tasks, frees tid_info and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original (success with tasks NULL returns 0 without filling tasks) right: 1125-1126; round-15 (on qed_cxt_get_tid_mem_info failure it returns that rc, not qed_iscsi_stop's) right: 1135-1141. 2/2 right. Slice cut the head; real function 1102-1152.

name: qed_enable_msix
prose: Tries to enable MSI-X for a qed device (qed_main.c:555-602; slice cut the head). It sets msix_table[i].entry = i for i < in.num_vectors and calls pci_enable_msix_range between in.min_msix_cnt and in.num_vectors. If it got fewer vectors than requested, at least the minimum, and the count is not a multiple of cdev->num_hwfns, it disables MSI-X, rounds the count down to a multiple of the number of hwfns and calls pci_enable_msix_exact with that count (rc becomes the count on success). For a PF with rc > 0, or a VF with rc equal to the requested count, it records int_mode QED_INT_MODE_MSIX and out.num_vectors = rc and returns 0. Otherwise it logs 'Failed to enable MSI-X' and returns rc unchanged: a negative errno, or for a VF a positive count smaller than requested (in which case the vectors stay enabled), or 0 for a PF when rc was 0 (possible when min_msix_cnt is 0), which returns 0 although no MSI-X mode was recorded.
note: Reviewers: original (on VF failure with positive rc < cnt vectors remain enabled) right: 590, 595-601; round-15 (can return 0 without acceptance when min_msix_cnt is 0) right: rc == 0 on a PF reaches 601 with out.* not set. 2/2 right. Slice cut the head; real function 555-602.

name: _qed_mcp_cmd_and_union
prose: Sends one command to the management firmware (MFW) mailbox and waits for its response (qed_mcp.c:460-579; slice cut the head). The caller must not hold mcp_info->cmd_lock; the function takes it with spin_lock_bh. Phase 1 waits (up to QED_DRV_MB_MAX_RETRIES iterations, sleeping or busy-waiting depending on the CAN_SLEEP flag) until there is no pending command or the pending one completes; if qed_mcp_update_pending_cmd returns an error other than -EAGAIN (for example -EINVAL when it finds no matching element) it releases the lock and returns that error. If the mailbox stays occupied it logs and returns -EAGAIN. It then re-reads the offsets, increments the driver mailbox sequence number, adds a command element (-ENOMEM on failure, lock released), writes the command, releases the lock and polls for the response. In the polling loop an error from qed_mcp_update_pending_cmd other than -EAGAIN is returned after unlocking, leaving the command element on the pending list (it is not removed on that path). If the MFW does not respond in time it logs, prints CPU info, removes the element, blocks further commands unless AVOID_BLOCK is set, reports QED_HW_ERR_MFW_RESP_FAIL and returns -EAGAIN. On success it removes the element, unlocks, and clears the sequence number bits from p_mb_params->mcp_resp (mcp_resp &= FW_MSG_CODE_MASK) before returning 0; the error paths do not clear them.
note: Reviewers: original (omits -EINVAL propagated from qed_mcp_update_pending_cmd) right: 484-485, 536-537, 576-578; round-2 (on -EINVAL the pending command stays in cmd_list) right: 576-578 only unlocks; round-15 (annotation says mcp_resp has the sequence number cleared, but update_pending_cmd stores the full mcp_resp including seq) WRONG for the success return: 572 clears it before return 0; only error returns leave it uncleared. 2 right, 1 wrong. Slice cut the head; real function 460-579.

name: qed_spq_post
prose: Posts a slow-path queue entry to the firmware (qed_spq.c:830-930; slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL if p_hwfn or p_ent is NULL. If the device is in recovery (cdev->recov_in_prog) it sets a fake return code (qed_spq_recov_set_ret_code) and returns 0 without posting the entry or returning it to the pool. Otherwise it fills the entry (qed_spq_fill_entry), then under p_spq->lock adds it to the pending queue and calls qed_spq_pend_post; a failure of any of these goes to spq_post_fail, which returns the entry to the free pool (except when qed_spq_pend_post failed, where the failing entry is assumed to have been handled already and is not returned here) and returns the error. For non-blocking modes it returns 0 after unlocking; the entry may then sit on the pending list, the unlimited-pending list or the completion-pending list, to be freed by the completion path. For EBLOCK mode it waits with qed_spq_block; if the entry was on the unlimited-pending queue it frees that entry and continues with the entry that was actually posted; on a wait error it removes the entry from its list, updates the completion bitmap and returns the entry to the pool, returning the error; otherwise it returns the entry to the pool and returns rc (0).
note: Reviewers: original (recovery path returns 0 without posting or returning the entry) right: 846-859; round-2 (pend_post failure does not always consume p_ent; it may remain in pending) right: 880-888 (b_ret_ent false); round-15 (non-blocking success can leave p_ent in unlimited_pending, not only pending or completion_pending) right: 899-901 shows that queue exists. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 830-930.

name: qede_add_cls_rule
prose: ethtool handler that adds a classification (flow steering) rule on a qede device (qede_filter.c:2038-2097; the packet item is the body of this function and its name was elided). It takes the qede lock (__qede_lock) and releases it with __qede_unlock at the unlock label on every path. It returns -EPERM if edev->arfs is not set; the error of qede_flow_spec_to_rule if the flow specification cannot be translated; -EINVAL if a filter with the same tuple already exists; and -ENOMEM if it cannot allocate the filter node or the node's header buffer (freeing the node in the second case). Otherwise it records the rule location as sw_id and sets that bit in the filter bitmap, copies the tuple, sets the destination from the flow spec, builds a minimal header, and calls qede_enqueue_fltr_and_config_searcher; if that fails it returns its error (this function does not free the node on that path; whether the callee does was not read). On success it configures the aRFS filter and returns the result of qede_poll_arfs_filter_config (0 or its error).
note: Item was the body of qede_add_cls_rule; fixed under the real name per rule 6 (read 2038-2097). The old prose named it arfs_filter_add; that name is not in the file.

name: qede_init
prose: Module init function of the qede driver (qede_main.c:262-295; marked __init; slice cut the head). It logs the driver banner, initialises the forced-speed maps, and obtains the qed ethtool/eth operations into the global qed_ops with qed_get_eth_ops(); if that returns NULL it logs and returns -EINVAL. It then registers the netdevice notifier (qede_netdev_notifier) before registering the PCI driver; if the notifier registration fails it logs, calls qed_put_eth_ops() and returns -EINVAL. It registers qede_pci_driver with pci_register_driver; on failure it logs, unregisters the netdevice notifier, calls qed_put_eth_ops() and returns -EINVAL (the original errno is discarded). On success it returns 0. It reads and writes module-global state (qed_ops and the registered notifier/driver).
note: Contract removed per rule 4: the function touches global state and its return value is only 0 or -EINVAL because of module registration side effects. Slice cut the head; real function 262-295. Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: ql_alloc_mem_resources
prose: Allocates the DMA memory and buffer queues of a qla3xxx adapter (qla3xxx.c:2831-2920; slice cut the head). It sets num_lbufq_entries and lrg_buffer_len from the netdev MTU (NORMAL_MTU_SIZE or JUMBO_MTU_SIZE); any other MTU logs and returns -ENOMEM before allocating anything. It derives num_large_buffers, the final large-buffer length and max_frame_size, then allocates a coherent page for the shadow registers; if that fails it logs and returns -ENOMEM directly, with nothing allocated. Then, in order, ql_alloc_net_req_rsp_queues, ql_alloc_buffer_queues, ql_alloc_small_buffers, ql_alloc_large_buffers; each failure goes to a label and returns -ENOMEM: a request/response queue failure frees only the shadow page here (the callee is responsible for its own partial allocations); a buffer-queue failure frees the request/response queues and the shadow page; a small-buffer or large-buffer failure frees the buffer queues, the request/response queues and the shadow page (the small buffers are not freed when the large-buffer allocation fails). After initialising the large buffers it creates the send free list; if that fails it frees the send free list, the buffer queues, the request/response queues and the shadow page (the large buffers allocated earlier are not freed on this path). On success it sets rsp_current to the start of the response queue and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: round-1 (small buffers not freed on large-buffer failure, large buffers not freed on free-list failure) right: 2895-2898 uses err_small_buffers label that does not free small buffers, 2902-2903 err_free_list does not free large buffers; round-2 (on ql_alloc_net_req_rsp_queues failure only shadow DMA is freed here) right: 2880-2882, 2914-2917; round-15 (shadow allocation failure frees nothing) right: 2875-2878. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head.

name: qlcnic_sriov_set_vf_spoofchk
prose: ndo_set_vf_spoofchk handler of the qlcnic PF (qlcnic_sriov_pf.c:2023-2046; the packet item is the tail of this function and its name was truncated). It returns -EOPNOTSUPP if the adapter is not an SR-IOV PF, -EINVAL if vf >= sriov->num_vfs. If the VF's QLC_BC_VF_STATE bit is set (the VF driver is loaded) it logs that the change failed and returns -EOPNOTSUPP without changing anything. Otherwise it stores chk in the VF's vport spoofchk field and returns 0.
note: Item was the tail of qlcnic_sriov_set_vf_spoofchk; fixed under the real name per rule 6 (read 2023-2046).

name: rmnet_egress_handler
prose: Sends an skb out through the rmnet logical device's real device (rmnet_handlers.c:240-278; the packet item is the body without its head). It updates the socket pacing shift (sk_pacing_shift_update(skb->sk, 8)), remembers skb->dev as orig_dev, sets skb->dev to the private real_dev and reads the mux id. It looks the rmnet port up with rmnet_get_port_rcu (the caller must hold the RCU read lock); if there is none it drops the packet. It then calls rmnet_map_egress_handler: -ENOMEM drops the packet, -EINPROGRESS returns without transmitting (the packet was consumed or deferred by the callee), and any other result (including other errors) continues. On the normal path it calls rmnet_vnd_tx_fixup and dev_queue_xmit(skb). Dropping means incrementing the per-CPU tx_drops counter of the rmnet device and kfree_skb. It returns nothing.
note: Item was the body of rmnet_egress_handler; fixed under the real name per rule 6 (read 240-278). The old prose did not cover the -EINPROGRESS return or that other errors still transmit.

name: ravb_rx_gbeth
prose: NAPI RX processing for a Gigabit RAVB (ravb_main.c:799-947; slice cut the head). It loops over at most limit = dirty_rx + num_rx_ring - cur_rx descriptors of queue q, advancing priv->cur_rx[q] for every loop iteration, stopping at the budget, at a DT_FEMPTY descriptor or when the limit is reached. A zero-length descriptor (a DMA-mapping error marker) is skipped. Receive error status bits update the error counters and the buffer is skipped. Otherwise it syncs the buffer, and for DT_FSINGLE/DT_FSTART it builds an skb with napi_build_skb (on failure it counts an rx_error, returns the page to the page pool and jumps to refill, leaving priv->rx_1st_skb unchanged and ending the loop); DT_FSTART also saves the skb in priv->rx_1st_skb; DT_FMID/DT_FEND add the buffer as a fragment to rx_1st_skb, or, if there is none, count an error, release the page and continue. A finished packet (DT_FSINGLE or DT_FEND) is passed through eth_type_trans, the gbeth checksum helper when NETIF_F_RXCSUM is set, counted and handed to napi_gro_receive, clearing rx_1st_skb. The buffer's page pointer is cleared as consumed. After the loop (also on the allocation-failure jump) it refills the ring with ravb_rx_ring_refill(GFP_ATOMIC), advancing dirty_rx, adds the received packet count to the queue's rx_packets statistic and returns the number of packets handed up.
note: Reviewers: round-2 (napi_build_skb failure goes to refill instead of continuing) right: 863-869; round-15 (rx_1st_skb not set to NULL on DT_FSTART allocation failure) right: 863-869 leave it as is. The checksum claim in round-2 (strips 4 bytes, sets UNNECESSARY) concerns ravb_rx_csum_gbeth, which I did not read. 2 right, 1 not checked. Slice cut the head; real function 799-947.

name: rocker_switchdev_event_work
prose: Workqueue handler that applies a queued switchdev FDB event on a rocker port (rocker_main.c:2714-2749). It takes rtnl_lock for the duration of the switch (the lock is not held on entry). For SWITCHDEV_FDB_ADD_TO_DEVICE it does nothing unless the entry was added by the user and is not local (without any debug message); otherwise it calls rocker_world_port_fdb_add and, only if that succeeds, notifies the offload with rocker_fdb_offload_notify; a failure is only logged with netdev_dbg and nothing is retried. For SWITCHDEV_FDB_DEL_TO_DEVICE it applies the same user/local guard and calls rocker_world_port_fdb_del, logging a failure (with the text 'fdb add failed'). It unlocks rtnl, frees the copied fdb address and the work item and drops the device reference taken by the notifier with dev_put. It returns nothing.
note: Reviewers: original (FDB op may fail and is only logged) right: 2730, 2741; round-15 (guard-false ADD path emits no debug message) right: 2726-2727. 2/2 right.

name: rocker_switchdev_event
prose: Switchdev notifier callback of the rocker driver (rocker_main.c:2752-2799). It returns NOTIFY_DONE immediately if the notifier's net_device is not a rocker port. For SWITCHDEV_PORT_ATTR_SET it returns whatever rocker_switchdev_port_attr_set_event returns (the notifier error code derived from the attribute set). For any other event it first allocates a work item with GFP_ATOMIC; if that fails it returns NOTIFY_BAD (this happens for every non-attribute event, including unknown ones). For SWITCHDEV_FDB_ADD_TO_DEVICE and DEL_TO_DEVICE it copies the FDB info, allocates a separate 6-byte address buffer (on failure it frees the work item and returns NOTIFY_BAD), copies the address, takes a device reference (dev_hold) and queues the work on the rocker's ordered workqueue, then returns NOTIFY_DONE. For an event that is neither of those it frees the work item and returns NOTIFY_DONE.
note: Reviewers: original (omits the SWITCHDEV_PORT_ATTR_SET return via the attr-set helper) right: 2763-2764; round-15 (an allocation failure for an unknown event returns NOTIFY_BAD, not NOTIFY_DONE) right: 2767-2769 returns NOTIFY_BAD before the event switch. 2/2 right.

name: sxgbe_xmit
prose: ndo_start_xmit of the Samsung sxgbe driver (sxgbe_main.c:1277-1432; slice cut the head). The queue is chosen by skb_get_queue_mapping(skb). It requests a context descriptor when the skb is GSO with a changed MSS, has a VLAN tag, or needs a hardware timestamp. If the TX path is in LPI mode it disables EEE mode. If the ring has fewer than nr_frags + 1 free descriptors it stops the queue (logging once) and returns NETDEV_TX_BUSY without consuming the skb. Otherwise it records the skb in tx_skbuff[entry]; for a GSO skb it writes the context descriptor when the MSS changed (advancing cur_tx and saving prev_mss) and calls sxgbe_tso_prepare; for a non-GSO skb it maps the linear data with dma_map_single (a mapping error is only logged and the descriptor is still prepared) and prepares the first descriptor. For each page fragment it advances cur_tx, maps the fragment, prepares the descriptor and sets its owner after a barrier. It then closes the last descriptor, updates the frame count and interrupt-coalescing bit, sets the owner of the first descriptor, advances cur_tx, stops the queue when the free descriptors fall to MAX_SKB_FRAGS + 1 or fewer, adds skb->len to tx_bytes, marks hardware timestamping in progress when requested, starts the DMA transmission for the queue and returns NETDEV_TX_OK. DMA mapping errors never cause the skb to be freed or the function to return an error.
note: Slice cut the head; real function 1277-1432. Old prose unreviewed; I rechecked the paths (notably mapping errors are only logged, 1351-1353, and the fragment mapping is not checked at all).

name: sxgbe_rx
prose: NAPI receive loop of the sxgbe driver (sxgbe_main.c:1486-1550; slice cut the head). It processes descriptors of the queue priv->cur_rx_qnum starting at cur_rx while count < limit and the descriptor is not owned by the hardware. Every descriptor it takes is counted in count and cur_rx is advanced before the status is examined, so the returned value counts descriptors examined, including ones with a negative status (skipped with continue) and a descriptor with no skb attached (logged as inconsistent and then the loop ends with break, after count was incremented). For a good descriptor it detaches the skb from the ring, sets its length from the frame length, sets ip_summed from the hardware checksum result (CHECKSUM_NONE when RX checksum insertion is off) and passes it up with netif_receive_skb for CHECKSUM_NONE or napi_gro_receive otherwise. After the loop it refills the RX ring with sxgbe_rx_refill and returns count (0 <= count <= limit).
note: Reviewers: round-1 (return counts descriptors examined, including negative-status and missing-skb cases) right: 1506, 1517-1520, 1526-1529, 1549; round-2 (a descriptor with a missing skb is counted before the break) right: 1506 precedes 1526. 2/2 right. Slice cut the head; real function 1486-1550.

name: efx_ef10_handle_rx_event
prose: Handles one EF10 hardware RX event for a channel (ef10.c:2808-2947; slice cut the head). It returns 0 immediately if efx->reset_pending is set. It decodes the event (bytes, next pointer low bits, queue label, L3/L4 class, continuation flag, encapsulation header class when the VXLAN/NVGRE capability exists), warns on a DROP event, and if the event's queue label differs from the channel's RX queue it calls efx_ef10_handle_rx_wrong_queue (which schedules a reset) and continues. It computes n_descs from the next pointer and the queue's removed_count. If n_descs is not scatter_n + 1: when n_descs == scatter_n it is an RX abort (warning if scatter_n is 0 or bytes are non-zero) handled by efx_ef10_handle_rx_abort and returns 0; otherwise merged completion is only accepted if the firmware reports RX_BATCHING and the packet is not scattered (scatter_n == 0 and not a continuation), else it calls efx_ef10_handle_rx_bad_lbits and returns 0; an accepted merge sets scatter_n to 1 and n_packets to n_descs. Otherwise it adds the descriptor to the scatter state and returns 0 for a continuation event, or n_packets = 1 for a final one. It then derives checksum flags from the error bits (efx_ef10_handle_rx_event_errors) or from the L4 and encapsulation classes (warning on an unknown encapsulation), adds the TCP flag for TCP, updates irq_mod_score, calls efx_rx_packet for each packet advancing removed_count, resets scatter_n and scatter_len, and returns n_packets.
note: Reviewers: original (abort path also computes n_descs and updates scatter state) right: 2847, 2861; round-2 (wrong-queue path only schedules reset and continues; n_descs computed after) right: 2844-2848; round-15 (merged completion does not require the RX_BATCHING capability) WRONG: 2869-2871 reject merged completion when the capability bit is absent. 2 right, 1 wrong. Slice cut the head.

name: efx_ef10_sriov_set_vf_mac
prose: Sets the MAC address of a VF from the PF (ef10_sriov.c:487-551; slice cut the head). It returns -EOPNOTSUPP if nic_data->vf is NULL and -EINVAL if vf_i >= efx->vf_count; a negative vf_i is not rejected. If the VF's own efx is attached it detaches and stops it, removes its filter table and frees its vadaptor (a failure returns that error with the VF left stopped). It then assigns the null EVB port to the VF (error returned), deletes the old MAC from the vport if it is non-zero (error returned), and, if the new MAC is non-zero, adds it to the vport (a failure zeroes vf->mac and returns the error) and sets the VF netdev's address when the VF efx exists. It stores the MAC in vf->mac, reassigns the EVB port to the vport (failure zeroes vf->mac and returns the error), and if the VF efx exists reallocates the vadaptor (error returned), re-probes the filter table, opens the netdev and attaches the device. It returns 0 on success. Failures after the detach leave the VF stopped.
note: Reviewers: original (negative vf_i is not rejected; only vf_i >= vf_count returns -EINVAL) right: 496; round-15 (precondition requires vf_i < vf_count but code returns -EINVAL for vf_i >= vf_count) right: 496-497. 2/2 right. Slice cut the head; real function 487-551.

name: __efx_siena_filter_rfs_expire
prose: Expires aged-out accelerated-RFS filters of a siena channel (siena/rx_common.c, 'bool __efx_siena_filter_rfs_expire(struct efx_channel *channel, unsigned int quota)' at about lines 994-1035, built only with CONFIG_RFS_ACCEL; the packet item is its last lines). It returns false at once if efx->rps_mutex cannot be taken with mutex_trylock. Otherwise it walks channel->rps_flow_id from channel->rfs_expire_index, wrapping at max_rx_ip_filters, and for each valid flow id decrements the quota and calls the type's filter_rfs_expire_one; when that returns true it logs, marks the slot RPS_FLOW_ID_INVALID and decrements rfs_filter_count. It stops when the quota is used up or after one full pass of the table. It stores the next index in channel->rfs_expire_index, unlocks efx->rps_mutex and returns true.
note: Item was the tail of __efx_siena_filter_rfs_expire; fixed under the real name per rule 6 (read 994-1035). The old prose described only the last three lines.

name: efx_neigh_event
prose: Processes a neighbour-table update for sfc TC encap actions (tc_encap_actions.c:521-585; slice cut the head). It always returns NOTIFY_DONE. If efx->tc is NULL it WARNs and returns. It accepts only neighbours of the ARP table (or the IPv6 ND table when enabled), otherwise returns without effect. A neighbour with no parms, or whose table key length does not match the expected size, logs a warning and returns. It reads the neighbour's MAC and validity under its lock, builds the key (net, destination address) and looks it up in efx->tc->neigh_ht under rcu_read_lock; if there is no binder or it is dying it does nothing. Under the binder's write lock, if the validity and MAC are unchanged it returns with no update. Otherwise it stores the new n_valid and MAC in the binder first, then, only if a reference can be taken (refcount_inc_not_zero), it drops the RCU lock and schedules the binder's work item; if scheduling fails (work already queued) it drops the reference it took and frees the binder if that was the last one. If the reference could not be taken the binder's data has already been updated but no work is scheduled.
note: Reviewers: original (omits no-change path) right: 566-570; round-2 (n_valid/ha are updated before refcount_inc_not_zero) right: 571-574; round-15 (missing parms or bad key_len log warnings, so not 'no side effects') right: 541-550. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 521-585.

name: ioc3eth_remove
prose: Platform-driver remove function of the SGI IOC3 Ethernet (ioc3-eth.c:965-976; returns nothing). It takes the net_device from platform_get_drvdata(pdev) and its private data with netdev_priv, but this file's probe never calls platform_set_drvdata, so the value is whatever drvdata the device holds (NULL if nothing else sets it, in which case the following ip-> accesses dereference a bad pointer). It frees the RX ring and the TX ring with dma_free_coherent, unregisters the netdev, deletes the timer synchronously and frees the net_device. The platform device's drvdata is not cleared afterwards. The DMA rings are freed before the netdev is unregistered.
note: Reviewers: round-1 (drvdata not cleared, leaving a dangling reference) wrong in its premise: drvdata is never set in this file (no set_drvdata call found), so nothing dangles from probe, though it is also not cleared here; round-2 (precondition assumes get_drvdata returns the netdev but probe never calls platform_set_drvdata) right; round-15 (unset drvdata causes a NULL deref before the rings are freed) right if the drvdata is NULL (967-970). 2 right, 1 wrong. Slice cut the head; real function 965-976.

name: stmmac_xdp_xmit_zc
prose: Submits AF_XDP zero-copy TX descriptors for one stmmac queue (stmmac_main.c:2499-2619; slice cut the head). queue's xsk_pool must be set. It refreshes the TX watchdog (txq_trans_cond_update), limits the budget to the free TX descriptors and then loops once per budget unit: if the free descriptors fall below STMMAC_TX_XSK_AVAIL or the carrier is down it clears work_done and stops; if xsk_tx_peek_desc returns no descriptor it stops with work_done unchanged; a descriptor longer than the EST max SDU for the queue is counted as dropped and skipped with 'continue', which still consumes one unit of budget (the for-loop decrement runs). Otherwise it fills the next TX descriptor (extended, TBS or basic layout), records it as an XSK TX buffer, sets the interrupt-on-completion bit by the coalescing count (also through the XSK TX metadata request), prepares the descriptor, enables DMA transmission and advances cur_tx. After the loop it adds the number of interrupt bits set to the TX statistics, and if at least one descriptor was filled flushes the descriptors and calls xsk_tx_release. It returns true only if budget is still non-zero and work_done is true; so it returns false when the budget was used up (including when the initial budget was 0) or when it stopped for lack of space or carrier, and true when it stopped because the XSK queue was empty with budget left.
note: Reviewers: round-2 (EST max-SDU skip uses continue in the for loop, so it consumes budget) right: 2517, 2535-2540; round-15 (work_done remains true when the budget is exhausted or initial budget is zero; annotation says false) mixed: work_done does stay true in those cases (2509, 2528 only sets false in the no-space case) but the function's return value is false because of '!!budget &&' at 2618. 1 right, 1 mixed. Slice cut the head; real function 2499-2619.

name: stmmac_napi_poll_rxtx
prose: NAPI poll callback for a combined RX/TX (XSK zero-copy) stmmac channel (stmmac_main.c:5858-5909; the packet name stmmac_poll is not a function and the slice starts inside this function). It increments the NAPI poll counters of the channel's RX and TX statistics, cleans completed TX descriptors with stmmac_tx_clean (limiting its result to the budget), receives with stmmac_rx_zc, and takes the larger of the two counts. If that count is at least the budget it returns budget and keeps polling. Otherwise it calls napi_complete_done; if that returns true it re-enables the channel's RX and TX DMA interrupts under ch->lock. If TX packets remain pending it arms the TX timer, and it returns min(work done, budget - 1).
note: Item named stmmac_poll does not exist; the slice 5869-6132 begins in stmmac_napi_poll_rxtx (5858-5909) and continues into other functions. I fixed it under that name; the old prose could not be matched to a single function with certainty. Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: tc_taprio_configure
prose: Applies a taprio offload request to the stmmac EST (enhanced scheduled traffic) hardware (stmmac_tc.c:966-1126; slice cut the head). It returns -ERANGE if qopt->base_time is negative, -EOPNOTSUPP if EST is not supported or the EST width/depth capability values are not recognised, and then, for TAPRIO_CMD_DESTROY, goes straight to the disable tail. For other commands it returns -EINVAL if there are more entries than the supported depth, -ERANGE if the cycle time is zero or the cycle-time extension does not fit, and -ENOMEM if priv->est cannot be allocated. These early validation returns do not disable EST. Once validation of the structural limits passes, it zeroes any existing priv->est and sets its size and enable flag under est_lock, and then validates each gate-control entry (-ERANGE for an interval or gate mask that does not fit, -EOPNOTSUPP for an unknown command); these per-entry failures return directly after priv->est was already cleared and partly filled, without disabling EST. It then computes the base time and cycle registers from the PTP clock, maps the per-queue max SDU, and calls stmmac_est_configure; a failure logs and goes to disable; it also maps the preemptible traffic classes (failure goes to disable) and returns 0. The disable tail, if priv->est exists, clears the enable flag, reprograms EST, resets the per-queue drop and hold statistics, and maps preemption classes to none; it returns that last mapping's result for TAPRIO_CMD_DESTROY and the earlier ret otherwise.
note: Reviewers: original (early validation returns do not disable EST, contradicting on-failure disable) right: 976-1024; round-2 (entry validation failures occur after priv->est is zeroed and enable set, so existing EST state is not untouched) right: 1035-1044, 1050-1065; round-15 (priv->est not left zeroed on a late failure: earlier gcl entries remain written) right: 1068. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 966-1126.

name: fflp_early_init
prose: Initialises the NIU/Neptune flow classifier (FFLP) once per parent (niu.c:3179-3236; slice cut the head). It takes the parent lock with niu_lock_parent and releases it with niu_unlock_parent at the common exit on every path. If PARENT_FLGS_CLS_HWINIT is already set in parent->flags it does nothing and returns 0. Otherwise, only for platform types other than PLAT_TYPE_NIU, it resets the FFLP, sets its timings and calls fflp_disable_all_partitions (a failure is logged and returned). For all platforms it then calls tcam_early_init (error logged and returned), enables LLC/SNAP and the error disable, clears the H1/H2 polynomial registers, calls tcam_flush_all (error logged and returned), and, again only for non-NIU platforms, clears the FCRAM hash (fflp_hash_clear; error logged and returned). It then clears the VLAN table and sets PARENT_FLGS_CLS_HWINIT. On an error the flag stays unset and the function returns that error; on success it returns 0.
note: Reviewers: round-1 (FCRAM hash clear only for non-NIU plat_type) right: 3219-3227; round-2 (fflp_disable_all_partitions only writes partition 0 repeatedly) right: niu.c:3128-3138 calls fflp_set_partition(np, 0, 0, 0, 0) FCRAM_NUM_PARTITIONS times; round-15 (it cannot return -EINVAL) unchecked: the error depends on fflp_set_partition, which I did not read. 2 right, 1 unchecked. Slice cut the head; real function 3179-3236.

name: happy_meal_init
prose: Brings a Sun HappyMeal Ethernet chip to the running state (sunhme.c:1256-1529; slice cut the head). It deletes the auto-negotiation timer, sets HFLAG_INIT on the first call (reading the hardware counters then; there is no early return when the flag was already set), stops the chip and reinitialises the TX/RX descriptor rings (happy_meal_init_rings, which cannot fail here), selects frame or bit-bang MIF mode, checks the transceiver and configures the Big MAC by transceiver type. It returns -EAGAIN if the transceiver type is 'none' or if happy_meal_tcvr_reset fails. It then resets the Big MAC TX/RX, programs inter-packet gaps, the MAC address, hash filter, DMA and burst configuration and the ERX configuration (a mismatch in the ERX config readback is only logged: 'XXX Should return failure here'), enables promiscuous or multicast filtering as the device flags dictate, sets the XIF configuration, enables TX and RX with the larger 802.1q frame size, starts auto-negotiation (happy_meal_begin_auto_negotiation) and returns 0. This function does not allocate rings and has no -ENOMEM return.
note: Round-15 reviewer (omits -ENOMEM from happy_meal_alloc_rings failure and the early return when HFLAG_INIT is already set) is WRONG for this code: there is no ring allocation or HFLAG_INIT early return in 1256-1529; the only error returns are the two -EAGAIN at 1307 and 1323. Slice cut the head. I read the head (1256-1335) and tail (1455-1529) and skimmed the middle (1335-1455: MAC, DMA and burst setup) without reading it line by line.

name: xlgmac_drv_probe
prose: Common probe for the Synopsys XLGMAC Ethernet driver (dwc-xlgmac-common.c:226-270; slice cut the head). It allocates a net_device with alloc_etherdev_mq (on failure it logs and returns -ENOMEM), sets the device, stores the netdev as the device's drvdata, fills xlgmac_pdata (device, netdev, IRQ and MAC register base taken from res, rss_mutex, message level), calls xlgmac_init (a failure logs 'xlgmac init failed' and goes to err_free_netdev) and register_netdev (a failure logs and also goes to err_free_netdev). err_free_netdev calls free_netdev and returns that step's error. On success it returns 0. It does not itself map registers or request the IRQ: res already supplies the IRQ number and mapped register base, and any failure to obtain them is outside this function.
note: Round-15 reviewer (omits -ENODEV, ioremap and IRQ failure paths; claims only -ENOMEM or xlgmac_init/register_netdev errors) is WRONG about this function: it has exactly the three error exits listed (232-237, 252-256, 258-262); the other failures belong to the caller that fills struct xlgmac_resources. Slice cut the head; real function 226-270.
